canonical.sourceFilePath: 11. Binary Trees/2. Medium Problems/11. Left or Right View.cpp

narrative.title: The Balcony Spotlight Pass
narrative.scenario: A theater's rigging grid hangs as a binary tree of light battens, and the lighting director watches from the right balcony. On every tier, battens farther left are blocked by the first one in the line of sight, so only the rightmost batten of each tier shows. The cue sheet lists the visible batten numbers from the top tier down.
narrative.inputFormat: The root of a binary tree given as a level-order array where null marks a missing child.
narrative.outputFormat: Return an array: the rightmost node's value on each level, ordered top to bottom.

testCases.explanation: Tier two shows 3 (its rightmost), and tier three shows 4 even though 5 exists on the left.
Each tier has exactly one visible batten.

hintLevels: Level 1: One survivor per level — the node standing last when the level is read left to right.
Level 2: During a size-sliced BFS, the node at position size-1 is the level's survivor.
Level 3: Flipping the direction (or recording the first node instead) turns this into the left view with the same skeleton.
